topicName: Field Types, Options, and Database Constraints
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Field Types, Options, and Database Constraints in Django"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Django models are the single, definitive source of information about your data. They contain the essential fields and behaviors of the data you are storing. Understanding field types, field options, and database constraints is fundamental to building robust and scalable web applications."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Core Field Types"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Django provides a rich set of built-in field types to handle various data formats. Choosing the correct field type ensures proper data validation, form generation, and database column mapping."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"CharField: For short, string-based data. Requires a max_length argument."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"TextField: For large text blocks. Maps to TEXT types in most databases."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"IntegerField / FloatField / DecimalField: For numerical data. DecimalField requires max_digits and decimal_places."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"BooleanField: For true/false values."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DateTimeField / DateField / TimeField: For handling dates and times with optional auto_now or auto_now_add parameters."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"from django.db import models

class Article(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    content = models.TextField()
    rating = models.DecimalField(max_digits=3, decimal_places=2)
    is_published = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Common Field Options"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Field options are arguments passed to field constructors to configure how the field behaves across the application, from forms to database migrations."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"null=True: If True, Django will store empty values as NULL in the database. Default is False."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"blank=True: If True, the field is allowed to be blank in forms and admin panels. Default is False."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"default: Provides a default value for the field. Can be a value or a callable function."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"choices: A sequence of 2-tuples to use as choices for this field, limiting inputs to predefined options."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"class Order(models.Model):
    STATUS_CHOICES = [
        ('PENDING', 'Pending'),
        ('SHIPPED', 'Shipped'),
        ('DELIVERED', 'Delivered'),
    ]
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=STATUS_CHOICES, default='PENDING')"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Database Constraints"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Database constraints enforce data integrity directly at the database level. Django allows you to define constraints using options on fields or via the Meta class using UniqueConstraint and CheckConstraint."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"unique=True: Ensures the value in this column is unique across the entire table."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"db_index=True: Tells Django to create a database index for this field, improving query speed."},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"For complex rules spanning multiple columns, use the Meta.constraints attribute."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"class Product(models.Model):
    store_id = models.IntegerField()
    sku = models.CharField(max_length=50)
    price = models.DecimalField(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [
            models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['store_id', 'sku'], name='unique_store_sku'),
            models.CheckConstraint(check=models.Q(price__gt=0), name='price_positive')
        ]"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"By correctly leveraging Django field types, options, and database constraints, you ensure that your application maintains high data integrity, runs optimized queries, and cleanly maps Python logic to your underlying database."}]
